ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Symptoms after an unplanned interruption

A 38-year-old woman stable on buprenorphine treatment abruptly stops taking it. She later develops sweating, abdominal cramps, and restlessness. There is no fever or recent infectious exposure. Which pharmacologic principle best explains this presentation?

  1. Chronic partial agonist exposure can produce physical dependence
  2. Partial agonists never produce physical dependence
  3. Withdrawal proves that prescribed treatment was ineffective
  4. Physical dependence is identical to compulsive drug use
  5. Abrupt cessation increases continuing mu-receptor activation
Answer and explanation

Chronic partial agonist exposure can produce physical dependence

Buprenorphine can produce dependence and withdrawal after abrupt cessation.

Option explanations

Chronic partial agonist exposure can produce physical dependence: Buprenorphine can produce dependence and withdrawal after abrupt cessation.

Partial agonists never produce physical dependence: Partial agonist activity does not rule out dependence.

Withdrawal proves that prescribed treatment was ineffective: Withdrawal reflects adaptation, not necessarily failure of treatment.

Physical dependence is identical to compulsive drug use: Dependence and the behavioral disorder of addiction are distinct concepts.

Abrupt cessation increases continuing mu-receptor activation: Stopping exposure reduces, rather than increases, ongoing agonist activation.
